security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL implements the pre-v0.8.1 HWCFG register layout (HWCFG0 holding chk_x, peis, pees, sps_en, stall_en, mfr_en, no_x, no_w, mdcfg_fmt, srcmd_fmt, mfr_en at their old bit positions) while advertising IOPMP spec v0.8.1 compliance. Under this condition, firmware writing HWCFG2 or HWCFG3 to configure security-critical features (instruction-fetch checking, per-entry interrupt/error suppression, write-access denial) programs the wrong register offset or bit position, leaving the actual hardware control bits at their reset values in HWCFG0. Conversely, reading HWCFG2/HWCFG3 to audit the current hardware enforcement state returns values from the wrong register, misleading software into believing protections are active when they are not.
security_spec.summary: Spec v0.8.1 massively reorganizes HWCFG register bit-fields across HWCFG0/HWCFG2/new-HWCFG3 and shifts ENTRYOFFSET from 0x14 to 0x2C; hardware implementing the old layout would silently misconfigure instruction-fetch checking (chk_x), per-entry interrupt/error suppression (peis/pees), write denial (no_w), and error capture (mfr_en), enabling DMA initiators to bypass IOPMP access controls.
